title: Warm-cache resonance exploration — perf scratchpad
content:
Goal:
Quick practical exploration of short-burst (10s–90s) latency changes when we intentionally 'resonate' the KV prefix cache by replaying synthetic similar prefixes across slightly-shifted contexts. Want to understand: does aggressive prefix reuse reduce p99 without hurting p50/p95? Are there pathological cases where cache resonance creates microbursts of GC/eviction pressure that increase tail?

Background / why: 
- Observed small improvements in token cost with prefix caching, but inconsistent tail behavior during mixed traffic.
- Hypothesis: when many requests re-hit same prefix keys in quick succession, we see improved amortized CPU but potential memory thrash if cache eviction/compaction hits.
- This doc is an ad-hoc lab log: replicate pattern, measure p50/p95/p99, map to cache hit-rate and free memory curve.

Experiment setup (short):
- Model: rwd-llama-13b-quant (local test build with kernel-opts from PR 2713)
- Instance: g4dn-like test box (1x A10G equivalent), 64GB RAM available to runtime
- Runtime flags: --kv-cache-size=12GB, --cache-policy=LRU, --batcher=continuous, batch-window=8ms (default)
- Load driver: drv-perf (internal harness) v0.9.1, 50ms client think-time configurable
- Request profile: short prompts (~40 tokens), 80% share of prefixes A/B (A is 60% of traffic, B is 20%, rest random)
- Concurrency targets: 40, 80, 160 concurrent connections (ramp and hold)
- Burst pattern: 10s microburst every 60s for 15 minutes run; separate run with sustained 90s burst every 300s
- Observed signals: qps, p50/p95/p99 latency (response complete), KV cache hit-rate (per prefix key), runtime RSS, GC/eviction logs

Runs and raw-ish observations:
1) Baseline (no resonance overlay) — 40 concurrency, steady Poisson arrivals
- qps: ~320 rps
- kv-hit-rate: ~18%
- latency: p50 24ms, p95 67ms, p99 180ms
- notes: stable, low RSS variance, no eviction spikes

2) Resonance short-burst (replay identical prefix sets at 10s windows) — 40 concurrency
- qps: burst to 420 rps during 10s windows, average 350 rps overall
- kv-hit-rate: jumps to 62% during burst, falls to 20% between bursts
- latency: p50 22ms, p95 58ms, p99 210ms (p99 increased vs baseline)
- runtime RSS: +~1.8GB during burst, slow decay (1.8 -> 1.2GB over 40s)
- eviction events: small thrash recorded at burst end (LRU scanning logs show ~80k entries considered)
- quick thought: high hit-rate lowers avg latency but p99 increased — likely eviction/compaction after burst

3) Resonance long-burst (90s resonance) — 40 concurrency
- qps: sustained ~410 rps during 90s
- kv-hit-rate: ~70% sustained
- latency: p50 20ms, p95 54ms, p99 160ms (improved p99 relative to short-burst)
- runtime RSS: grows more (peak +3.6GB), but compaction happens during quieter windows in this run
- observation: longer resonance seems to allow cache steady-state to form; eviction compaction happens less aggressively because workloads stay warm instead of oscillating

4) Higher concurrency (160) with short-burst resonance
- qps: burst peaks ~1600 rps
- kv-hit-rate: 55% during burst
- latency: p50 36ms, p95 120ms, p99 540ms (severe tail)
- runtime RSS: peak +6GB, multiple eviction cycles recorded, kernel OOM killer not hit but process had long pauses (~200–500ms sampling) correlating with p99 spikes
- note: at high concurrency bursts, cache manager and batcher contend for CPU; GC compaction becomes synchronous-ish causing head-of-line stalls

Mini-charts (ASCII) — p99 across representative runs (normalized):
- baseline: |===----| 180ms
- short-burst 40c: |==------*| 210ms
- long-burst 40c: |==--| 160ms
- short-burst 160c: |=====---------| 540ms

What I think is happening (working hypothesis):
- Micro resonance (brief, frequent bursts) causes repeated eviction/rehydration cycles: cache fills quickly during burst, then eviction scanner/compactor kicks in to reclaim space leading to CPU+memory pressure and long tail pauses.
- Longer resonance windows let the cache reach a more stable allocation; background compaction can be amortized and p99 improves.
- At high concurrency, the batcher/runtime scheduling interacts badly with cache compaction: CPU saturation shifts compaction into the foreground, increasing pause times.

Quick experiments to validate (next runs):
- Disable synchronous compaction (soft-disable) + run short-burst at 160c to see if p99 drops. (linked to PR 2713 flag)
- Try cache-policy=segmented-LRU (if available in branch) to reduce thrash for small hot sets.
- Reduce batch-window to 4ms to see if smaller batches reduce head-of-line during compaction at high concurrency.
- Increase kv-cache-size to 18GB and re-run short-burst at 160c to test if capacity reduces eviction frequency (cost vs tail tradeoff).

Anomalies / oddities observed:
- One run showed p99 spikes that did not align with eviction logs but did show a spike in page-faults (major, measured via /proc). Suspect kernel-level memory pressure from other services in testhost — need to isolate with cgroup-limits next.
- Some requests had very low latency but anomalously high token counts (possible client harness bug — counting tokens twice). Filed JIRA-RT-1528 for follow-up.

Notable logs / pointers:
- grep of eviction scanner: runtime/kv_cache/evict.go: logs at 2026-01-30T15:02:12Z show 82k scanned, reclaimed 640MB
- PR that changes kernel opts: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2713
- Slack thread: perf-warm-cache (see pinned messages around 2026-01-30)

Quick conclusions (working):
- Warm-cache resonance is not unilaterally good: micro-resonance can increase p99 due to eviction/compaction thrash.
- Longer sustained reuse windows produce better amortization and improved tails.
- High concurrency amplifies the negative interaction; need scheduler-level mitigations (background compaction + compaction backoff) and sizing/capacity levers.

TODO / next steps:
- [ ] Run "disable-sync-compaction" experiment (PR flag) at 160c short-burst — measure p99 and RSS curve. (Owner: Fenton)
- [ ] Try segmented LRU policy (if branch exists) — ask @Maya to spin up variant. (Owner: Maya)
- [ ] Isolate testhost with cgroups, re-run anomalous-case. (Owner: Omar)
- [ ] Add microprofile tracer spans for cache eviction path (low overhead sampling) — open GH issue if not present.

Notes to self: keep these runs reproducible: commit run-id, harness branch, exact runtime binary sha in next iteration. Save full raw logs to s3://perf-archives/warm-resonance/2026-01-30/ (will upload after verification).

End of scratchpad.
